title: UK government replaces Palantir software with internally-built refugee system
summary: The UK government has replaced Palantir's controversial data analytics software (used for immigration enforcement) with a domestically-built system for processing refugees and asylum seekers, marking a shift toward digital sovereignty in sensitive government operations.
problem_solved: The UK government reduced its dependency on a US defense contractor for sensitive immigration data processing and gained more control over critical national infrastructure.
why_valuable: This demonstrates a growing trend of governments seeking digital sovereignty by building in-house solutions instead of relying on foreign commercial vendors for sensitive public sector data operations.
